title: Written arrangements, heads and copying solos in the early bands
summary: Early bands mixed written parts and heads, each thought its own style the best, and players copied others' solos such as Bunny Berigan's Singin' the Blues.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: These bands that we've been talking about, the early bands that you played in, did they mostly...if they had arrangements, were they heads? Or did they play from written...?
Some of them had written things. Some had heads. Always play...(?)... to learn to read, you know.
And mostly each band had its own, or at least tried to have its own style?
Everybody had their own little thing, and they thought they were hot stuff, everybody in ...(?)...
Would there be much of what you might call improvised solo playing in those days? Or was it mostly a matter of taking a break or a few bars or something in...?

Yes, there was much improvising. Not all the time, no. Guys would take something somebody else had played, they'd heard play, you know, and put it in there. It's like they used to play a very good solo on... They thought it was a really great thing to do, you know. They did "Singin' The Blues." It was a masterpiece thing, like everyone wants to play it... Today they try to play it... [SINGS A REFRAIN] And ...(?)... has been recorded(?). But invariably they want to play his solo. Everybody...you know... But it's Bunny Berrigan they're playing really. It's a theme, it's a nostalgic theme, and it's... It's like Tommy Dorsey playing. Everybody wants them to play exactly like they played it.
That's the way it was in those days, too, because you'd hear somebody play something, and...you know, copy it. It would help them learn(?) (?) a great deal.
And then the guy who copied it would be the one who became famous for it.
Sometimes. You don't hear hardly anything that... You don't hear some of Louis' things in anybody's solo. I don't care who plays it. You're going to hear some
of Louis Armstrong, you know. That's the way it is. Is that ...(? )...?
